cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Christ, haloed, sits on a green globe holding out a long scroll, flanked by an angel at the right and two saints at the left. The verse above calls to 'exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at his footstool'.
facts: Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature.

cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-129-de-pr.summary: At the bottom of the drawing the psalmist, surrounded by four demons brandishing a scroll, a trident, a serpent and a frog, calls out from a pit: 'out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord'. Above, the cross-nimbed Christ-Logos, with a cross-staff and six angels, holds out a scroll toward a group of Israelites, while the sun and moon mark the watch 'from the morning ... until the night'. It is the upper drawing of folio 74v, the De profundis.
facts: The Utrecht Psalter illustrates every psalm and canticle with a lively pen drawing — 166 in all — that translates the words of the text, often literally, into images; in these the Lord of the psalms is regularly shown as the youthful Christ-Logos.
Its text is written in rustic capitals, an archaic script that once led scholars to date the manuscript to the 6th century; the drawings are now recognised as Carolingian.
cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-129-de-pr.notes: The figure of the Lord is identified as Christ (the Christ-Logos) following the commentary of the Utrecht University Library's annotated edition, which describes the psalter's consistent practice of drawing the God of the psalms as the youthful Christ. The image is a crop of the drawing from the library's IIIF image server. This folio carries two drawings; the crop shows the one for this text.

Q561341.summary: At the centre of this jewelled gold cover Christ sits in majesty, raising his hand in blessing and holding an open book on his knee. Around him, embossed gold reliefs show the four evangelists, each with a scene from his Gospel, framed by raised settings of sapphires, emeralds and pearls. It is one of the very few treasure bindings to survive from the 9th century, a cover worthy of the King whom the Gospels proclaim.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the cover can be precisely dated to 870 and was made for Charles the Bald in his 'Palace School', whose location, perhaps Saint-Denis, is uncertain.
The book on Christ's knee is inscribed with his words 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life', so that the verse can be read as spoken by Christ or by the Gospel book itself.
The four scenes are Christ and the woman taken in adultery, the expulsion of the money-changers, the healing of the blind man and the healing of the leper.
